# Modal Provider Skills

## Component Overview

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Type token prefix | `modal:index:` |
| Resources | `Secret`, `Volume`, `Queue` |
| Upstream API | Modal gRPC control-plane (`github.com/modal-labs/modal-client/go/proto/modal_proto`) |
| Auth | `x-modal-token-id` / `x-modal-token-secret` gRPC metadata, injected per-RPC. Token lookup: resource inputs, `modal:tokenId`/`modal:tokenSecret`, `MODAL_TOKEN_ID`/`MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET`, then the `~/.modal.toml` profile (`MODAL_CONFIG_PATH`, `MODAL_PROFILE`, else `active = true`); the profile's `environment`/`server_url` apply only when it supplies the credentials |
| pulumi-go-provider | `infer` package (native provider) |
| Resource count | 3 |

## Architecture

This is a **native provider** (not a TF bridge — Modal has no Terraform provider to
bridge from). It uses `pulumi-go-provider`'s `infer` package and talks directly to
Modal's public gRPC control-plane API via the generated Go protobuf client
(`modal-client/go/proto/modal_proto`). All RPC calls go through `pkg/provider/client.go`,
which wraps the generated stub with per-RPC credential injection via a unary
interceptor. There is no separate HTTP client — Modal's control plane is gRPC-only.

## Resource Behavior Matrix

| Resource | Create | Read | Update | Delete |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Secret | `SecretGetOrCreate` (`CREATE_FAIL_IF_EXISTS`) | `SecretGetInfo` (by ID; keys and environment, never values) | `SecretUpdate` (values only, in place) | `SecretDelete` |
| Volume | `VolumeGetOrCreate` | `VolumeGetById` | `VolumeRename` (name only; environment/fsVersion force new) | `VolumeDelete` |
| Queue | `QueueGetOrCreate` | `QueueGetById` | **N/A — replace only** (name/environment force new) | `QueueDelete` |
| Dict | `DictGetOrCreate` | `DictGetById` | **N/A — replace only** (name/environment force new) | `DictDelete` |
| Environment | `EnvironmentCreate` | `EnvironmentList` (by ID) | `EnvironmentUpdate` (name, web suffix, task and GPU limits) | `EnvironmentDelete` |
| App | `AppGetOrCreate` (`CREATE_FAIL_IF_EXISTS`) | `AppGetInfo` + `AppList` + `AppGetTags` | `AppSetTags` (name/environment force new) | `AppStop` |
| Image | SDK `Build` (`ImageGetOrCreate`, `ImageJoinStreaming`) + `ImagePublish` | `ImageFromId` + `ImageListTags` | `ImagePublish` + `ImageNameDelete` (published name only; build inputs force new) | `ImageNameDelete` + `ImageDelete` |

`Secret.values` updates in place (`SecretUpdate` diffs old vs. new keys and sends per-key
upserts/deletes) and `Volume.name` renames in place (`VolumeRename`). Queue has no update
RPC and Secret has no rename RPC, so every other change forces a replace.

Read always goes by ID (`SecretGetInfo`, `VolumeGetById`, `QueueGetById`) so refresh and
import work from the ID alone. Modal does not report a Volume's or Queue's environment:
Create records the effective environment in state, and import looks in the configured
(or default) environment and verifies the ID matches.

## Force-Replace Rules

- **Secret.name** — replace (no rename API)
- **Secret.environment** — replace
- **Volume.environment** — replace
- **Volume.fsVersion** — replace, delete-before-replace when name and environment are unchanged (changing FS backend requires a new volume and loses data)
- **Queue.name** — replace
- **Queue.environment** — replace

`Secret.values` and `Volume.name` diff to in-place updates; every other field forces
replacement.

**Never name an input `version`**: pulumi-go-provider drops it before Diff
(pulumi/pulumi-go-provider#704), so Volume uses `fsVersion`.

## Development Workflow

| Step | Command | When to run |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `go mod tidy` (provider root) | Fresh checkout, after adding new dependencies |
| 2 | `go build ./...` (provider root) | After code changes |
| 3 | `go test ./...` (provider root) | Always before committing |
| 4 | `gofmt -l .` (provider root, must be empty) | Always before committing |

**Go toolchain**: `$HOME/go-toolchain-1.25/bin/go` (Go 1.25.8). Add it to `PATH`, not
`$HOME/go-toolchain-1.25/go/bin/go` — that nested path does not exist on this
workstation image.

**Build verification sequence**:

```bash
export PATH=$HOME/go-toolchain-1.25/bin:$PATH
go mod tidy
go build ./...
go vet ./...
go test ./... -v
gofmt -l .
```

## Common Mistakes

| Mistake | Consequence | Correct approach |
|---|---|---|
| Passing `*ProviderConfig` where a value is expected | Type mismatch — `infer.GetConfig` returns a value, not a pointer | `clientFor(cfg ProviderConfig, ...)` takes a value receiver |
| Assuming `grpc.NewClient` dials eagerly | Believing client construction needs network access (breaking unit tests) | `grpc.NewClient` is lazy without `WithBlock()` — safe to construct in tests with fake credentials |
| Calling `Volume`/`Queue` `Update` | No such method exists — these resources are create/read/delete only | Any field change other than what's absent from `Diff`'s `ForceReplace` set is impossible; every field currently forces replace |
| Forgetting the `SecretUpdate` nil-value-means-delete convention | Silently fails to remove a key from a Secret | Send `pb.SecretUpdateRequest_Update_builder{Key: k, Value: nil}` to delete a key, not an update with an empty string |
| Using `$HOME/go-toolchain-1.25/go/bin/go` | `No such file or directory` | Correct path is `$HOME/go-toolchain-1.25/bin/go` |

## API Quirks

### Secret API

- **Get-or-create semantics on Read**: `SecretGetOrCreate` with
  `ObjectCreationType: OBJECT_CREATION_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED` is used for *both* Create (with
  `CREATE_FAIL_IF_EXISTS`) and Read (unspecified — tolerant of an already-existing
  object). This mirrors the Modal Python SDK's `Secret.from_name(..., create_if_missing=...)`
  pattern.
- **Values are secret**: The `values` map is tagged `provider:"secret"` — every value is
  encrypted in the Pulumi state file, not just token credentials.
- **Env var key validation**: Secret keys must match `^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*$` (mirrors
  Modal's own server-side validation) — enforced client-side in `client.go` before the
  RPC to fail fast with a clear error instead of a generic gRPC `InvalidArgument`.
- **Update deletes by omission is NOT how it works**: `Update` diffs old vs. new key
  sets and explicitly sends a `nil`-value update for keys present in the old set but
  missing from the new one; it does not send a bulk replace.

### Volume API

- **Two filesystem backends**: `fsVersion` selects `VOLUME_FS_VERSION_V1` (legacy) or
  `VOLUME_FS_VERSION_V2` (default, recommended). Passing an unrecognized string returns
  `VOLUME_FS_VERSION_UNSPECIFIED` plus an error — validate before the RPC.
  Filesystem version cannot be changed on an existing volume, hence force-replace. When omitted we create v2 (Modal's Go SDK would default to v1; we keep v2 so existing programs do not change).
- **No content management via this provider**: This resource manages the durable
  Volume object itself (existence, name, environment, FS version) — file contents are
  written/read by Modal Functions at runtime via the Modal Python/JS/Go client
  libraries, not by Pulumi.

### Queue API

- **No capacity or retention config exposed**: The gRPC `QueueGetOrCreate` API only
  takes name/environment — there is no `maxSize`, `ttl`, or similar field to
  provision. Do not invent one; if a future Modal API version adds queue-level config,
  extend `QueueArgs` then.
- **FIFO/LIFO behavior is a client-side property**, not a create-time provider setting —
  callers choose ordering with `queue.get(..., partition=...)` semantics at the Modal
  client level, not via this Pulumi resource.

## Dict, Environment, App, Image (v0.2 coverage)

- **Coverage inventory**: `research/coverage/modal.md` lists every SDK service and RPC group with a class
  (resource, lookup, runtime, deferred, out of scope) and a reason. Update it when the pinned SDK moves or a
  resource is added.
- **Environment** is workspace-level and has no `environment` input. Modal has no get-by-ID: Read lists
  environments and matches the ID. Everything updates in place (`EnvironmentUpdate`).
- **App** creates only the empty named App. Delete is `AppStop`; a stopped App reads as gone. The name is not in
  the handle metadata, so Read lists the environment's Apps to find it.
- **Image** builds through the SDK (`modal.NewClientWithOptions` with our authenticated stub as
  `ControlPlaneClient`), so layer handling and the build-log stream stay upstream's. The stream needs the auth
  stream interceptor in `client.go`. A build needs an App: the provider creates `pulumi-image-builds`. Deleting
  an Image only removes the published name while it still points at this image, because a replacement may
  already have taken the name. Imported Images have no build inputs (`baseImage` unset) and Diff ignores build
  inputs in that case.
- **Lookups** (`functions.go`) use the lookup-only creation type, so they never create. Do not add a lookup that
  needs `GetOrCreate` semantics.
- **Never name an input `version`** (see the Force-Replace Rules note).


## WebhookToken (#1536)

- **WebhookToken** has no get-by-ID RPC either: Read scans `WebhookTokenList`. Outputs are `webhookTokenId` and the write-once
  secret `webhookTokenSecret` (create only; Read and Update keep the stored one; an import has none). `name` updates through
  `WebhookTokenUpdate`; `scoped` replaces. `WebhookTokenEnvironment{Add,List,Remove}` (attaching a scoped token to environments by
  environment ID) is not modelled yet. `getWebhookToken` looks up by name and fails when the name is not unique.

## Proxy, ServiceUser, AppDeployment (#1445)

- **Proxy** and **ServiceUser** have no get-by-ID RPC: Read scans `ProxyList`/`ServiceUserList` for the ID. Proxy
  `ipCount` is the only in-place input (`ProxyAddIp`, `ProxyRemoveIp` takes the IP, not the proxy ID); a failed resize
  returns the proxy in state with `ResourceInitFailedError` so a retry resizes it rather than leaking addresses.
- **ServiceUser** outputs are named `serviceTokenId`/`serviceTokenSecret` because `tokenId`/`tokenSecret` are the
  resource-level API credentials. The secret exists only in the create response; Read keeps the stored one.
- **AppDeployment** runs the Modal CLI. Credentials, environment and endpoint reach it through the process environment
  (`credentialsFor` in `provider.go` resolves them like `clientFor`), never argv. Failure output is redacted of the token
  pair and the `env` values. Tests use a fake `modal` shell script (`fakeCLI`) plus the fake control plane; the script
  cannot create the App, so tests seed it in the fake before Create.
- The fingerprint (`sourceFingerprint`) is computed in Diff as well as Create, so editing source shows as an update at
  preview time. A missing source directory fingerprints to "" and does not diff.


## Domain (#1538)

- Modal has only `DomainCreate`, `DomainList` and `DomainCertificateVerify`: no get-by-ID, no update, no delete. Read scans
  `DomainList` for the ID; `getDomain` scans by name (case-insensitive) or ID.
- Delete only forgets. So Create adopts a domain that is already registered under the same name (it logs a warning), which
  keeps destroy followed by up working. Do not add a delete call: there is none.
- `verify` is the only in-place input. It calls `DomainCertificateVerify` on create, update and refresh while the status is not
  issued; a failed check on refresh keeps the values just read, a failed check on create keeps the domain in state with
  `ResourceInitFailedError` so a retry verifies it.
- The properties are `domainName` and `domainId`, never `domain` (a property named like its resource breaks C# codegen).
